title: Remediate event-delivery work identity and scheduling authority
businessObjective: Prevent queue-state corruption and caller-controlled scheduling in the bounded Phase 3 event-delivery core before workflow runtime work begins.
technicalObjective: Make work IDs unique, derive due-time decisions from the trusted clock port, snapshot validated outbound-port configuration at construction, and carry queue idempotency identity through dispatch without introducing a provider, transaction, or production integration.
architectureReferences: docs/architecture/source/Sri U-Thong Grand Hotel AI OS.md
assumptions: P3-002 is terminal on origin/main and its historical packet and evidence remain immutable.
The module remains Tier-0/shadow and non-authoritative; no production write, deployment, credential access, or live provider is authorized.
Dispatch-before-persist is retained as an explicit at-least-once shadow limitation; exactly-once delivery requires a future transactional/outbox adapter task.
The existing admitted npm validator and verify:task mapping are sufficient; this remediation does not change verifier admission or CI.
acceptanceCriteria: submit rejects a new request whose workId already exists under a different idempotencyKey with deterministic WORK_ID_CONFLICT, while an exact idempotency replay remains idempotent and cannot create a second record.
Stored duplicate work IDs are treated as invalid persistence and fail closed; runDue updates only the selected batch records and cannot apply one dispatch result to an out-of-batch or future record.

runDue obtains its scheduling timestamp only from the trusted clock port; caller-supplied timestamps are rejected or ignored without authority, a far-future caller value cannot dispatch future work, and invalid or unavailable clock output fails closed.

After construction, mutations or replacement of the caller's limits, clock, storage, or dispatcher properties do not change the validated configuration used by the module; the captured limits and callable ports are frozen/snapshotted.

Dispatcher input includes the queue idempotencyKey for every work item, and documentation states the current dispatch-before-persist behavior is at-least-once in Tier-0/shadow mode with no exactly-once claim or production adapter authority.

Focused regression tests cover duplicate work IDs, caller-clock disagreement, post-construction port mutation, idempotency-key propagation, persistence failure after dispatch, malformed inputs, and the existing event-delivery contract without introducing infrastructure imports or production behavior.
allowedCommands: npm run verify:task -- --task SUT-AIOS-P3-002-R01 --base origin/main --verifier-agent qa-verification --verifier-model gpt-5.6-sol --acceptance-confirmed
solEscalationTriggers: Any change requires a database, queue, workflow, provider, transport, transaction, outbox, credential, deployment, booking, payment, pricing, inventory, authorization, RLS, or production path.
Any proposed behavior would allow caller input, adapter output, or provider state to become scheduling, execution, approval, or policy authority.
Any exact-once or cross-process delivery guarantee is requested beyond the bounded idempotency-key propagation and documented shadow limitation.
rollbackExpectations: Revert the remediation branch and generated artifacts while preserving the terminal P3-002 packet, all historical evidence, and any blocked verification records.
